title: Does sharing cut how much the sharer uploads?
takeaway: With 5 viewers on the same connection, the person sharing the video uploaded 500% of what one viewer watched when everyone downloaded from them, and 102% when viewers passed the video on to each other.

title: Does the sharer upload more as more people watch?
takeaway: As the room grew from 2 to 10 viewers, the sharer's upload stayed between 100% and 111% of what one viewer watched; without sharing it would grow to 1000%.

title: How closely in step do the screens stay?
takeaway: 99% of the time, viewers' screens were within 17 ms of each other, about one screen refresh, with no network trouble, with 5% of data lost and with everyone 25 ms delayed; with one viewer 60 ms farther away than the rest, within 43 ms.

title: How full does the sharer's connection get?
takeaway: With 5 viewers on a 10 Mbit/s connection, sending everyone their own copy would need 132% of it, more than it has; off-the-shelf sharing settings kept it 99% full, and this app used 30%, with the same smooth, in-step playback.

title: After the sharer's connection drops, do viewers keep freezing? This app against its own earlier version
takeaway: After the sharer's connection dropped from 10 to 1 Mbit/s for about 2 minutes and came back, viewers froze 2, 0, 0 times with this app's current version and 109, 20, 35 times with its earlier version in side-by-side tests.

title: How long does a viewer wait?
takeaway: With 5 viewers, the video was playing for everyone about 4.8 s after pressing play and 5.0 s after jumping to a new point; someone joining late was playing in step after 3.1 s.

title: Does sharing still work on weaker connections?
takeaway: When the sharer uploads at 5 Mbit/s, viewers still got 79% of the video from each other, and when one viewer uploads at 1 Mbit/s, 67%; nobody froze in these tests.
